baseline.reason: The agent claim lacks a matching admissible three-version oracle.; The task's bug is a pure JS logic error: CurlUtils.escapeStringWin() in devtools/client/shared/curl.js used a `\s`-based safe-character allowlist that over-matches whitespace-like control characters (tab, form feed, vertical tab, CR, etc.), letting them pass through unescaped into generated Windows cmd.exe/curl command lines, enabling command injection (reporter's PoC used a fetch body containing \t, \r, \n around calc.exe). The fix (5c7b1adb9c3f) replaces those whitespace-like control characters with a plain space before escaping. To verify this behaviorally I needed to build the target (pre_intro, post_intro, post_benign) and run a self-checking PoC that invokes escapeStringWin on a string containing a tab/CR/LF around a payload and checks whether the dangerous characters survive unescaped in the output. However, build_version failed identically on all three revisions: after a normal configure, mach build died ~1:15-1:17 into compilation of toolkit/library/rust (third_party/rust/neqo-crypto) with 209 Rust errors about missing NSS symbols (PR_Now, PR_ErrorToString, SSL_OptionSet, NSS_SetDomesticPolicy), which is nowhere near the devtools JS code and is unrelated to the single-regex-character patch. Since this is a shared/global build failure (same error, same stage, same unrelated subsystem, across pre_intro/post_intro/post_benign), it reflects a broken build environment rather than anything the patch touches. Per the ground rules I did not retry the unchanged build repeatedly beyond confirming the failure on each version, did not edit the tracked target source or shared Rust/NSS dependency to force a fix, and did not substitute a locally repaired source tree. With no version buildable, run_poc and docker_shell also refuse to execute (gated on build success), so no PoC could be run on any revision, the SAME-command invariance requirement cannot be satisfied, and I cannot judge introduction or benignness from any actual target execution. Recording intro_verified=unknown and benign_verified=unknown, consistent with the instruction to record unknown for an untested label rather than infer a verdict from a failed/unrelated build.
